correctness.rationale: The phase for candidate \(k\) is \(j/k\); reduced-denominator \(q\) probes exactly test \(q\mid k\). Adjacent prime-power candidates \(p^{a-1}\) and \(p^a\) require a reduced-denominator \(p^a\) probe. All prime powers suffice by unique factorization. Confinement to denominator-\(H\) grid forces every prime power to divide \(H\), equivalent to the lcm condition. For common timing tolerance \(\varepsilon<1/(2N^2)\), distinct reduced fractions are separated by at least \(1/N^2\), so a probe cannot cover two mandatory prime-power witnesses; proposed exact phases retain the same incidence vector. Both upper/lower bounds are proved for every integer \(N\ge2\). Exact finite checker confirms 11025 ancillary assertions but is not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The naturally arising unpruned period-alias family produces a complete exact survey-design problem. The theorem supplies the globally minimum number of fixed photometric checks, distinguishes universal identification from certifying only the longest period, proves persistence for a quantitative positive transit half-duration, and gives a necessary-and-sufficient exact regular-cadence obstruction. At N=38 the contrast between 19 flexible checks and an exact grid of 5.34 quadrillion subdivisions is a meaningful warning against conflating rigid cadence with phase targeting, not a claim that real instruments require this resolution. The result is motivated by published duotransit follow-up difficulties and can guide theoretical benchmark tests while explicitly disclaiming practical calibration.
